headline: DEA registers 900+ medical dispensaries, then limits who they can trade with
dek: Federal protection arrives for a fraction of applicants, with a supply-chain rule that could split state markets in two.
body: The DEA has granted federal registration to more than 900 of roughly 7,000 priority applicants under the new medical rescheduling framework. Jushi Holdings is among the companies confirming registrations.

The catch: registered businesses may only buy from and sell to other registered or timely-applied companies, and have until late November to rework their sourcing. The agency also says it cannot register operators in states with dual medical and adult-use licenses, or in states that let patients self-certify.
Expect a scramble for compliant supply partners this month, and a widening gap between medical-only states and mature adult-use markets.
